The bank column of a business cash book showed a debit balance of $25000. The following was then discovered. $ direct debit payments not recorded in the cash book 6500 payments for sales made directly into the bank by 5500 customers but not recorded in the cash book bank charges not recorded in the cash book 1500 payment made by the business but not yet shown in 4500 the bank statement What was the correct cash book balance?

It would normally sell for $2400 but can now only be sold for $2200 if repairs costing $400 are undertaken. What value of the damaged inventory should be shown in the financial statements?

At 31 December 2019 X, Y and Z were in partnership sharing profits and losses equally. At that date the net assets of the partnership were valued at $300000 and X’s capital account balance was $70000. On 1 January 2020 X retired. The net assets were then revalued upwards by $90000. X left half of the amount due to him on retirement as a loan to the partnership. What was the value of the partnership’s net assets remaining after X’s retirement?
